items.stem: At which layer of the TCP/IP model does IP addressing and routing operate?

options.rationale: Correct: IP addressing and routing between networks live at the internet/network layer.
The application layer handles protocols like HTTP, not IP routing.
The link layer handles local delivery and MAC addressing, not routing between networks.
The transport layer handles TCP/UDP segments, not IP routing.

items.explanation: Correct: IP addressing and inter-network routing happen at the internet/network layer.

items.stem: Which TWO statements correctly contrast TCP and UDP? (Select TWO)

options.text: TCP provides ordered, reliable delivery with acknowledgements
options.rationale: Correct: TCP guarantees ordered, acknowledged delivery.

options.text: UDP has lower overhead and no built-in delivery guarantee
options.rationale: Correct: UDP is connectionless with minimal overhead and no reliability guarantee.
UDP does not retransmit; that is a TCP feature.

items.explanation: Correct: TCP is reliable and ordered; UDP is lightweight and connectionless.

items.stem: A user can reach a server by IP address but not by its hostname. What is the most likely cause?

options.rationale: Correct: reachability by IP but not by name points to DNS resolution.
The IP connection works, so the physical link is fine.
The host already has a working address, so DHCP is not the issue here.

options.text: A depleted CPU on the client
options.rationale: CPU load would not selectively break name resolution.

items.explanation: Correct: working IP connectivity with failing name access indicates a DNS issue.
